answer: Florida Medicaid covers up to 24 hours of private duty nursing per day at home when the care is medically necessary, does not duplicate another service, requires more extensive and continual care than a home health visit, can be safely provided at home, and the recipient is under a licensed practitioner's care. The passages do not state Medicare coverage for round-the-clock nursing for a ventilator patient.

citations.quote: Florida Medicaid covers up to 24 hours of PDN services per day, per recipient, in accordance with the applicable Florida Medicaid fee schedule, or as specified in this policy, when the recipient meets all of the following criteria:
Requires more extensive and continual care than can be provided through a home health visit

gold_answer: Florida Medicaid covers up to 24 hours a day of private duty nursing when the recipient needs more extensive and continual care than a home health visit can provide and the other criteria are met. Medicare does not pay for 24-hour-a-day care at home.
gold_quote: Florida Medicaid covers up to 24 hours of PDN services per day, per recipient, in accordance with the applicable Florida Medicaid fee schedule, or as specified in this policy, when the recipient meets all of the following criteria: || Medicare doesn’t pay for: • 24-hour-a-day care at home

judge.rationale: The answer correctly states that Florida Medicaid covers up to 24 hours of private duty nursing per day with the listed criteria, but it misses the gold's second part that Medicare does not pay for 24-hour home care, saying only that the passages don't address it; every claim it does make appears in P3.

question: Is round-the-clock nursing at home something either Florida Medicaid or Medicare will cover for someone on a ventilator?
